title: GIGABYTE’s GAIFA Opens in Taiwan: What a Vendor-Run AI Factory Data Center Tells Us About Buying AI Hardware
summary: A new kind of AI factory data center just came online in Tucheng, a district of New Taipei City, Taiwan. Giga Computing, GIGABYTE‘s enterprise server business, switched on a facility...
body_markdown:
A new kind of AI factory data center just came online in Tucheng, a district of New Taipei City, Taiwan. Giga Computing,[GIGABYTE](https://www.newegg.com/GIGABYTE/BrandStore/ID-1314?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_gigabytes-gaifa-opens-in-taiwan-what-a-vendor-run-ai-factory-data-center-tells-us-about-buying-ai-hardware) ‘s enterprise server business, switched on a facility it calls[GAIFA](https://www.gigabyte.com/press/news/2453?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_gigabytes-gaifa-opens-in-taiwan-what-a-vendor-run-ai-factory-data-center-tells-us-about-buying-ai-hardware) , short for *GIGABYTE AI Factory Accelerator*, in late September 2026. At first glance, it looks like any other GPU hall. However, GAIFA does not rent out compute or train models for the public. Its job is to run customer-style AI racks under full load so buyers can see what works before they spend. Here at Newegg Insider, we think that shift says a lot about where AI hardware is heading. Below, we break down what is inside, why the numbers matter, and how the same technology reaches the systems our shoppers buy every day.


## **GAIFA at a Glance**


GAIFA is a 700 kW, six-rack, liquid-cooled AI factory data center that Giga Computing uses to validate rack-scale AI systems with customers. The table below sums up the key facts.


Detail What Giga Computing announced


Initial scale Six racks for compute, storage, and networking


Power capacity 700 kW planned for the first phase


Cooling Direct liquid cooling across major compute platforms


GPU platforms NVIDIA GB300 NVL72, NVIDIA HGX B300, NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000


CPU platforms AMD EPYC blades, plus new 6th Gen AMD EPYC (SP7) servers


Purpose End-to-end validation, from one system up to a full cluster


In short, GAIFA is both a showroom and a test lab. Customers can watch a full AI rack run under real power and heat. That beats reading about it on a spec sheet.


## What’s Inside the AI Factory Data Center


**The facility mixes flagship NVIDIA rack systems, enterprise GPU servers, and dense AMD EPYC compute, so it covers nearly every tier of AI infrastructure.** Each platform maps to a different kind of buyer.


### NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 (two racks)


Two racks run the NVIDIA GB300 NVL72, the most integrated system in the building. Each rack links 72 Blackwell Ultra GPUs and 36 Grace CPUs into one liquid-cooled system. Giga Computing aims these racks at trillion-parameter model training and agentic AI. In other words, this is the tier that hyperscalers and large AI labs buy.


### G4L4-SD3-LAX7 with NVIDIA HGX B300 (one rack)


Next, one rack holds G4L4-SD3-LAX7 servers built on NVIDIA HGX B300 boards. These servers also use direct liquid cooling. However, they target enterprise AI teams that want dense GPU compute without buying a full NVL72 rack.


### XL44-SX2-AAS1 with NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000


The XL44-SX2-AAS1 carries eight NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPUs per system. It handles visual computing, generative AI inference, and professional graphics. Because it uses PCIe cards, it is the platform closest to what mid-size companies can deploy today.


### B683-Z80-LAS1 AMD EPYC blade


Finally, the B683-Z80-LAS1 is a 6U, liquid-cooled blade system with ten AMD EPYC sockets. It covers the quieter but essential jobs: host compute, virtualization, HPC, and AI inference. After all, every GPU cluster still needs strong CPUs to schedule work and move data.


## Why Liquid Cooling and 700 kW Matter


**GAIFA’s 700 kW budget works out to more than 100 kW per rack on average, a density that air cooling alone struggles to handle in an AI factory data center.** That one number explains why the whole facility runs on liquid.


For comparison, enterprise racks have long been planned around a small fraction of that power. Modern GPU racks change the math. A single NVL72 rack draws well over 100 kW, and HGX-class servers pull several kilowatts per node. As a result, operators must carry heat away with liquid, straight from the chips.


Liquid cooling brings its own challenges, though. Coolant distribution units, leak detection, quick-disconnect fittings, and plumbing all need testing together. That is exactly what GAIFA validates: compute, power, and cooling as one system. Consequently, customers can find a weak link before a rollout instead of after it.


## Validation as a Service: The Real Story Behind GAIFA


**The biggest shift is not the hardware but the model: server makers now sell proven, rack-level results instead of individual boxes.** GAIFA turns that idea into a building.


Giga Computing lists a broad validation scope. It covers GPU and CPU performance, rack power density, liquid cooling, interconnects, networking, and component compatibility. It also extends to real-world tuning and **L12 validation** , which means testing at the full cluster level.


“GAIFA is not just Giga Computing’s own AI compute center, it is a real-world proving ground where we validate AI infrastructure together with our customers,” said Daniel Hou, General Manager at Giga Computing.


This approach solves a real pain point. AI clusters fail in ways single servers never do. For example, one wrong cable, firmware version, or coolant setting can idle millions of dollars of GPUs. By testing full racks under load first, a vendor shortens the path from delivery to the first training run.


## The 6th Gen AMD EPYC Angle


**GAIFA also debuts Giga Computing’s first servers for 6th Gen AMD EPYC (EPYC 9006 Series), with SP7 systems shipping in November 2026 and SP8 systems in March 2027.** That gives the facility a forward-looking CPU story next to its GPU racks.


Two SP7 platforms stand out. The **R165-DG2-CS1** is a 1U single-socket server with closed-loop liquid cooling. According to Giga Computing, it runs the full 256-core SP7 chip at maximum power inside 1U. The **B685-D80-LS1** , on the other hand, is a 6U ten-node blade with direct liquid cooling for dense HPC.


These systems matter because AI factories are not just GPU farms. Host CPUs feed accelerators, run smaller inference models, and manage orchestration. With up to 256 cores and PCIe Gen 6 per socket, 6th Gen AMD EPYC adds CPU headroom to every rack. If you need EPYC capacity now, current[AMD EPYC server motherboards](https://www.newegg.com/p/pl?N=100007629+601407371&utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_gigabytes-gaifa-opens-in-taiwan-what-a-vendor-run-ai-factory-data-center-tells-us-about-buying-ai-hardware) and[EPYC-based servers](https://www.newegg.com/p/pl?d=epyc+server&utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_gigabytes-gaifa-opens-in-taiwan-what-a-vendor-run-ai-factory-data-center-tells-us-about-buying-ai-hardware) are available while the new generation ramps.


## How GAIFA Fits the Wider AI Factory Trend


**GAIFA follows a clear pattern: hardware vendors now build their own AI factory data centers to prove rack-scale designs before customers buy.** NVIDIA popularized the “AI factory” label for sites that turn data and power into trained models and tokens. Since then, server makers have raced to show they can deliver whole factories.


Three forces drive the trend. First, rack-scale systems like the GB300 NVL72 ship as whole units, so vendors must test them as whole units. Second, power and cooling now limit AI growth in many regions. Third, enterprise buyers want less risk, so they prefer to see a reference design running before they sign.


Taiwan adds another advantage. The island anchors much of the global server supply chain. Therefore, a validation site in New Taipei City sits close to the factories that build these racks, which speeds testing and shipping.


## Bring GAIFA’s Lessons Home: Systems You Can Buy Today


**Most companies will never build an AI factory data center, but the same GIGABYTE and NVIDIA technology is available at server, workstation, and single-card scale.** Here are three ways to follow GAIFA’s playbook, from a full GPU server down to one card.


GIGABYTE G494-ZB0-AAP2: an eight-GPU server like GAIFA’s XL44


The[GIGABYTE G494-ZB0-AAP2 HPC/AI server](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16816202459?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_gigabytes-gaifa-opens-in-taiwan-what-a-vendor-run-ai-factory-data-center-tells-us-about-buying-ai-hardware) is a 4U dual-socket system for AMD EPYC 9005 and 9004 processors. It holds up to eight dual-slot PCIe Gen 5 GPUs. That includes eight NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition cards, or eight H200 NVL GPUs with NVLink bridges. In other words, it matches the eight-GPU RTX PRO 6000 layout of GAIFA’s XL44 systems.


The supporting hardware is just as serious. The server offers 24 DDR5 RDIMM slots across 12 memory channels, two extra PCIe Gen 5 x16 slots for networking, and dual 10 Gb/s LAN ports. Four 3,000 W 80 PLUS Titanium power supplies provide redundancy. For GPUs, the passively cooled[RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition](https://www.newegg.com/nvidia-900-2g153-0000-000-rtx-pro-6000-96gb-graphics-card/p/N82E16814132104?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_gigabytes-gaifa-opens-in-taiwan-what-a-vendor-run-ai-factory-data-center-tells-us-about-buying-ai-hardware) is built for exactly this kind of chassis.


### GIGABYTE W775-V10-L01: GB300 on your desk


The same GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra technology in GAIFA’s NVL72 racks also ships in a deskside tower. The[GIGABYTE W775-V10-L01 AI Workstation](https://www.newegg.com/msi-ws300t60l-tower/p/N82E16859252054?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_gigabytes-gaifa-opens-in-taiwan-what-a-vendor-run-ai-factory-data-center-tells-us-about-buying-ai-hardware) uses the NVIDIA GB300 Desktop Superchip. It pairs a 72-core Grace CPU with one Blackwell Ultra GPU. Together, they share 748 GB of coherent memory: 252 GB of HBM3E at 7.1 TB/s, plus 496 GB of LPDDR5X.


That unified memory matters for AI developers. Because NVLink-C2C links the CPU and GPU, both work on the same data without copying it. As a result, large language models too big for a single PCIe card can run locally. The system is rated for up to 20 PFLOPS of AI performance. It also adds two 400 Gb/s QSFP ports through NVIDIA ConnectX-8, closed-loop liquid cooling, and a 1,600 W 80 PLUS Platinum power supply. It suits teams that prototype and fine-tune models before moving them to a cluster, or that must keep data on-premises.


### NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q: the single-card entry point


Not every team needs a server or a superchip, however. The[NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q Edition](https://www.newegg.com/nvidia-900-5g153-2200-000-rtx-pro-6000-96gb-graphics-card/p/N82E16814132105?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_gigabytes-gaifa-opens-in-taiwan-what-a-vendor-run-ai-factory-data-center-tells-us-about-buying-ai-hardware) packs 96 GB of GDDR7 ECC memory and 24,064 CUDA cores into a 300 W, dual-slot card with active cooling. Its lower power draw lets one workstation run up to four cards. It also supports Multi-Instance GPU, so one card can split into as many as four isolated instances.


### Planning tips before you buy


Whatever the scale, the same AI factory data center lessons apply.


- **Plan power first.** GPU systems can draw several kilowatts, so check circuits and cooling early.
- **Consider liquid cooling.** Dense GPU nodes in crowded racks run cooler and quieter with it.
- **Balance the system.** Pair GPUs with enough host cores,[server memory](https://www.newegg.com/Server-Memory/SubCategory/ID-541?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_gigabytes-gaifa-opens-in-taiwan-what-a-vendor-run-ai-factory-data-center-tells-us-about-buying-ai-hardware) , and fast[NVMe storage](https://www.newegg.com/p/pl?d=ssd&utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_gigabytes-gaifa-opens-in-taiwan-what-a-vendor-run-ai-factory-data-center-tells-us-about-buying-ai-hardware) .
- **Validate before scaling.** Test one full node under real load before ordering dozens.


To compare more options, browse Newegg’s[AI workstation store](https://www.newegg.com/AI-Workstation/EventSaleStore/ID-2711?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_gigabytes-gaifa-opens-in-taiwan-what-a-vendor-run-ai-factory-data-center-tells-us-about-buying-ai-hardware) ,[AI, ML, and HPC server barebones](https://www.newegg.com/p/pl?N=101714305+601451697&utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_gigabytes-gaifa-opens-in-taiwan-what-a-vendor-run-ai-factory-data-center-tells-us-about-buying-ai-hardware) , and[GIGABYTE server barebones](https://www.newegg.com/GIGABYTE-Server-Barebones/BrandSubCat/ID-1314-8?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_gigabytes-gaifa-opens-in-taiwan-what-a-vendor-run-ai-factory-data-center-tells-us-about-buying-ai-hardware) . Our deep dive on the[RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell workstation for local AI](https://www.newegg.com/insider/nvidia-rtx-pro-6000-blackwell-workstation-96gb-gddr7-for-serious-local-ai/?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_gigabytes-gaifa-opens-in-taiwan-what-a-vendor-run-ai-factory-data-center-tells-us-about-buying-ai-hardware) covers the card in more detail.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is GAIFA?


GAIFA, short for GIGABYTE AI Factory Accelerator, is Giga Computing’s first AI factory data center. It opened in New Taipei City, Taiwan, and validates rack-scale AI infrastructure with customers.


### How big is the GAIFA AI factory data center?


The first phase includes six racks for compute, storage, and networking, with 700 kW of planned power. Giga Computing designed it to expand in later phases.


### Which GPUs does GAIFA use?


GAIFA runs two NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 racks, one rack of NVIDIA HGX B300 servers, and XL44 systems with eight NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPUs each.


### Does GAIFA include AMD EPYC servers?


Yes. It includes an AMD EPYC blade system and new 6th Gen AMD EPYC SP7 servers. SP7 systems ship in November 2026, and SP8 systems follow in March 2027.


### Can I buy GIGABYTE AI hardware like GAIFA’s?


Yes, at smaller scale. The GIGABYTE G494-ZB0-AAP2 server supports eight RTX PRO 6000 GPUs, and the W775-V10-L01 workstation brings GB300 to a desk.


## Conclusion


Giga Computing’s GAIFA shows that the AI factory data center has become the new unit of competition in server hardware. Instead of selling boxes, vendors now prove full racks under real power, heat, and network load. With 700 kW, direct liquid cooling, NVIDIA’s latest GPUs, and new 6th Gen AMD EPYC servers, GAIFA covers the full stack.


Meanwhile, the same technology is reaching smaller teams through eight-GPU servers, GB300 workstations, and 96 GB professional cards. Plan power, cooling, and balance before you scale.
